f.x: Preferred emollients and soap substitutes: Epimax cream, ZeroAQS, Aquamax, Isomol gel, Zerodouble, AproDerm cream, Zerobase, Oilatum cream, emulsifying ointment, 50:50, Zeroderm and Hydromol ointment. The linked Leicestershire Emollient Formulary PDF dates from 2016. QV does not appear.

Creams: AproDerm, Aquamax, Epimax, Epimax Oatmeal and ExCetra, ZeroAQS, Zerobase, Zerocream. Gels: Epimax Isomol, AproDerm, Zerodouble. f.t: South West London ICB: SWL Joint Medicines Formulary: 13.02.01 Emollients
f.x: No tiers stated. Formulary products include Aquamax, Balneum Plus, Cetraben (noting Epimax ExCetra is more cost-effective in primary care), Epimax Original and Isomol, Zerobase, Zerocream, Zeroguent, emulsifying ointment, Epaderm, Hydromol, Fifty:50, Zeroderm and Dermol 500. QV does not appear.

f.t: Kent and Medway ICB: Emollient Prescribing Guidance for Adults and Children
f.x: Three columns: most, medium and least cost-effective, with *** marking preferred. Preferred: Epimax Original cream, Epimax Isomol gel, Epimax ointment, Epimax Oatmeal cream. Other most cost-effective: Epimax ExCetra, ExmaQS, Aquamax, EmulsifEss, Fifty:50. QV Cream and QV Lotion are in the least cost-effective column.
